CITY OF INGLEWOOD
  ECONOMIC AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT DEPARTMENT
  SPECIAL PLANNING COMMISSION
  MEETING AGENDA
April 12, 2023 7:00 P.M.
City Council Chambers – Ninth Floor
1 West Manchester Boulevard
----------------------------------------------------------------------

1.  Pledge of Allegiance.

2.  Roll Call.

3.  Communications from staff.

4.  Public Comments Regarding Agenda Items. Persons wishing to address
  the Planning Commission on any item on the agenda other than a
  public hearing may do so at this time.

5.  PUBLIC HEARINGS
  a. A public hearing to consider an application by Judy Lee for
  Special Use Permit No. 2022-011 (SP-2022-011) to allow:
  1) The construction of a new self-storage facility; and
  2) A reduced parking requirement through alternate modes of
  transportation on an M-1L (Limited Manufacturing) zoned
  property at 3846 West Century Boulevard.

  Preliminary Recommendations:
  a. Preliminary CEQA Recommendation: Affirm Notice of
  Exemption EA-CE-2022-146; and
  b. Preliminary Recommendation: Adopt Findings and the
  attached resolution approving SP-2022-011 subject to 12
  conditions.
  Item 5a Documents

  b. A public hearing to consider an application by Winston Liu for a
  Zoning Code Amendment to allow Automated Car Wash Facilities in
  the MU-C (Mixed-Use Corridor) zone as standalone uses (not
  ancillary to a service station)
  Preliminary Recommendations:
  a. Preliminary CEQA Recommendation: Affirm Notice of
  Exemption EA-CE-2023-013; and
  b. Adopt a Resolution Recommending approval of Zoning Code
  Amendment No. 23-00001.
  Item 5b Documents

6.  NON-PUBLIC HEARING
  a. A non-public hearing to consider an application by Judy Lee for
  Design Review No. 2022-014 (DR-2022-014) to allow the
  construction of a new 6-story, approximately 335,000 square-foot
  self-storage facility on an approximately 72,000 square-foot,
  M-1L (Limited Manufacturing) zoned property at 3846 West Century
  Boulevard.
  Preliminary Recommendations:
  a. Affirm the categorical exemption EA-CE-2022-146
  b. Adopt the attached resolution approving DR-2022-014
  subject to 8 conditions and/or add conditions as deemed
  appropriate.
  Item 6a Documents

7.  Commission Initiatives.

8.  Public Comments. Anyone wishing to address the Planning
  Commission on any matter within their jurisdiction and not
  elsewhere considered on the agenda may do so at this time.

  (Revised 4/10/23)
 9.  Adjournment.

If you will require special accommodations, due to a disability, please
contact the Planning Division at (310) 412-5230, One Manchester
Boulevard, Fourth Floor, Inglewood City Hall, Inglewood, CA 90301. All
requests for special accommodations must be received 48 hours prior to
the day of the hearing(s).

"Si no entiende esta noticia o si necesita más información, favor de
llamar a este número (310) 412-5230."

In the event that the Planning Commission meeting of April 12, 2023, is
not held, or is concluded prior to a public hearing or other agenda item
being considered, the public hearing or non-public hearing agenda item
will automatically be continued to the next regular Planning Commission
meeting.

MINUTES
  INGLEWOOD PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  WEDNESDAY, MARCH 1, 2023

(1) PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE:
The City of Inglewood Planning Commission held its Planning
Commission meeting on Wednesday, March 1, 2023, in the Council
Chambers, on the ninth floor, in City Hall. Following the Pledge
of Allegiance by Commissioner Patricia Patrick, the meeting was
called to order at 7:00 p.m.

(2) ROLL CALL:
Present: Chairman Larry Springs
  Commissioner Patricia Patrick
  Commissioner David Rice
  Commissioner Aidé Trejo
  Commissioner Cheryl Shaw-Williams

Staff:  Christopher E. Jackson, ECD Director
  Mindy Wilcox, AICP, Planning Manager
  Michael Pan, Assistant City Attorney
  Eddy Ikemefuna, Senior Planner
  Bernard McCrumby, Senior Planner
  Marissa Fewell, Planner
  Angel Leon-Martell, Assistant Planner
  Christine Rivera, Assistant Planner
  Sean May, Planning Technician
  Evangeline Lane, Secretary
  Boytrese Osias, CIP Manager, Public Works Dept. on
  behalf of Parks, Recreation and Community Services

(3) STAFF COMMUNICATIONS:
Ms. Wilcox, Planning Manager stated 1) Item 6A’s materials have
been revised ,posted on the City’s website, passed out to each
Planning Commissioner and a copy has been placed for the public.
The case planner will explain the changes in those materials during
their presentation; 2) The Planning Commission is invited to attend
this year’s Annual National American Planning Association
Conference in Philadelphia, next month – April 2023, and all
information will be given shortly.

(4) PUBLIC COMMENTS:
None.

(5) MINUTES:
Chairman Springs called for Minutes approval for the January 23,
2023 Special Planning Commission meeting and February 1, 2023,
Planning Commission Meeting.

MOTION:
Commissioner Trejo made the motion to approve the January 23, 2023
Special Planning Commission Minutes and seconded by Commissioner
Patrick.

Ayes:  Commissioners Patrick, Rice, Trejo, Shaw-Williams and
  Chairman Springs.

Commissioner Shaw Williams made the motion to approve the February
1, 2023 Planning Commission Minutes and seconded by Commissioner
Trejo.

Ayes:  Commissioners Patrick, Rice, Trejo, Shaw-Williams and
  Chairman Springs.
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
March 1, 2023
(6) PUBLIC HEARINGS:

6A. SPECIAL PERMIT USE NO. 2022-010 (SP-2022-010) 3111 WEST
CENTURY BOULEVARD: A public hearing to consider an application
by Carina Perez for Special Use Permit No. 2022-010 (SP-2022-
010) to allow the location of a 75-foot high, wireless
telecommunications facility (mono-palm) on a C-2 (General
Commercial) zoned property at 3111 West Century Boulevard.

Mr. Angel Leon-Martell, Assistant Planner, made the staff
presentation and described the revised materials which include
additional proposed antennas.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff.

Commissioner Rice asked staff-
 Why was the applicant increasing the operational capacity to an
  increase of 3X’s the initial request?
   Mr. Leon-Martell replied to Commissioner Rice’s question.

Commissioner Trejo asked staff-
 Per the plans, the one monopalm, was supposed to have 3
  antennas on that one palm, will this same monopalm now have 9
  antennas on the one palm instead?
  - Mr. Leon-Martell replied to Commissioner Trejo’s question.
  - Ms. Wilcox also replied to Commissioner Trejo’s question.
 The conditions that are being imposed include the number of
  palm fronds as 60+, and that was for three, are the palm fronds
  going to increase in order to cover all of the nine antennas?
   Mr. Leon-Martell replied to Commissioner Trejo’s question.
 If this is going to be approved in Site Plan Review, we want
  to insure that there are enough palm fronds to cover all of
  the antennas, also with security cameras, as we understand
  almost all of these antennas have security cameras.
 Next question is about parking, so with the increase of the
  panels and increase of ground equipment, will that take away
  any of the parking?
   Mr. Leon-Martell replied to Commissioner Trejo’s question.
 How will the increase of the new palm fronds that we are
  learning about tonight, take away from the parking at the site?
   Mr. Leon-Martell replied to Commissioner Trejo’s question.
   Ms. Wilcox also replied to Commissioner Trejo’s question.
Commissioner Rice asked staff-
 There is another Monopalm just west of this new project, and
  the camouflage regarding that particular monopalm is lacking
  of quality, what is the maintenance schedule required for this
  particular project?
   Ms. Wilcox replied to Commissioner Rice’s question.

Chairman Springs asked the applicant to come forward to address
the Planning Commission and speak about their project.

Mr. Alex Tsaturov, of Morrison Hershfield  representing  the
applicant addressed the Planning Commission.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for the applicant.

  2
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
March 1, 2023
Commissioner Rice asked the applicant –
 What is the saturation of the proposed monopalm and how many
  monopalms are you looking to bring into Inglewood and why?
   Mr. Tsaturov responded to Commissioner Rice’s question.
 This is for telephone coverage - correct? Also, wondering how
  many times you would be coming before the Planning Commission?
   Mr. Tsaturov responded to Commissioner Rice’s question.
 Where other than the local freeway are you looking to place
  your Monopalms and are there other sites and where?
  - Mr. Tsaturov responded to Commissioner Rice’s question.

Commissioner Trejo asked the applicant –
 Do your Monopalms provide coverage for other cities outside of
  Inglewood or for Inglewood only, and if yes who?
  - Mr. Tsaturov responded to Commissioner Trejo’s question.
 If this is approved, how long will it be before service is up
  and running?
  - Mr. Tsaturov responded to Commissioner Trejo’s question.
 So you are saying this is an FCC Mandate?
   Mr. Tsaturov responded to Commissioner Trejo’s question.

Chairman Springs opened the public hearing to the audience to
speak either for or against this project.

FOR / AGAINST:
None.

Chairman Springs closed the public hearing and asked if there
were any further questions from the Planning Commission.

Commissioner Rice asked a question to the applicant –
 How close are they to their goal of saturation in Inglewood?
   Mr. Tsaturov responded to Commissioner Rice’s question.

Chairman Springs closed the public hearing and called for a
motion.

MOTION:
Commissioner Trejo motioned to affirm categorical exemption EA-
CE-2022-139 and adopt the attached resolution approving SP-2022-
010 subject to the 24 conditions, and was seconded by Commissioner
Shaw-Williams, that Resolution No. 1952

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY PLANNING COMMISSION
  OF  THE  CITY  OF  INGLEWOOD,  CALIFORNIA,
  APPROVING A SPECIAL USE PERMIT TO CARINA
  PEREZ, REPRESENTING FULSANG FOR DISH WIRELESS,
  TO ALLOW THE LOCATION OF A 75-FOOT HIGH,
  WIRELESS TELECOMMUNICATION FACILITY (MONO-
  PALM) ON A SITE DEVELOPED WITH AN EXISTING
  SHOPPING CENTER ON A 30,940 SQUARE-FOOT C-2
  (GENERAL COMMERCIAL) ZONED PROPERTY LOCATED AT
  3111 WEST CENTURY BOULEVARD.

Be approved.

The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:

Ayes:  Commissioners Patrick, Rice, Trejo, Shaw-Williams and
  Chairman Springs.

Ms. Wilcox explained the appeal process.

March 1, 2023
(7) NON-PUBLIC HEARINGS:

7A. PLANNING COMMISSION REVIEW NO. 2023-002 (PCR-2023-002) NORTH
PARK, 625 EAST HARGRAVE. A non-public hearing to consider Planning
Commission  Review  2023-002  (PCR  2023-002)  to  allow  the
installation of a new playground canopy in North Park on an
approximately 2.3-acre site.

Ms. Christine  Rivera,  Assistant  Planner,  made  the  staff
presentation.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff.

Mr. Boytrese Osias, Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) Manager from
the Public Works Department, and also on behalf of Sabrina Barnes,
Director of Parks, Recreation and Community Services Department.

Commissioner Patrick asked the applicant –
 Is this is the first canopy in the City of Inglewood’s parks?
   Mr. Osias responded to Commissioner Patricks’ question.
 What was the cost and why has there been a delay in placing them
  in other parks in the City?
   Mr. Osias responded to Commissioner Patricks’ question.

Commissioner Rice asked the applicant –
 Are there any upcoming decisions or even in the near future,
  decisions to have these types of canopies in the Edward Vincent
  Park in the amphitheater area?
   Mr. Osias responded to Commissioner Rice’s question.

Commissioner Trejo asked the applicant –
 What is the life span for this type of Canopy?
  - Mr. Osias responded to Commissioner Trejo’s question.

Chairman Springs asked the applicant for clarification -
 Wanting to ensure he heard the true amount of the cost of the
  canopy, and just wondered why that particular material instead
  of a stronger material like steel or glass?
  - Mr. Osias responded to Chairman Springs’ question.
   Mr. Jackson responded to Chairman Springs’ question.

Commissioner Rice asked the applicant –
 Concerned about the actual coverage area of the Canopy, how does
  that cover the area fully and how can the City purchase a good
  quality canopy brand?
  - Mr. Osias responded to Chairman Springs’ question.

Chairman Springs closed the non-public hearing and asked if
there were any further questions from the Planning Commission,
seeing none, he called for a motion.

MOTION:
Commissioner  Shaw-Williams  motioned  to  affirm  categorical
exemption EA-CE-2023-004 and adopt the attached resolution
approving PCR-2023-002 subject to the 5 conditions, and was
seconded by Commissioner Patrick, that Resolution No. 1953

  4
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
March 1, 2023

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY PLANNING COMMISSION
  OF  THE  CITY  OF  INGLEWOOD,  CALIFORNIA,
  APPROVING A REQUEST TO INSTALL ONE (1) NEW
  PLAYGROUND CANOPY AT NORTH PARK ON AN
  APPROXIMATELY 2.3-ACRE SITE AT 625 EAST
  HARGRAVE STREET.

Be approved.

The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:

Ayes:  Commissioners Patrick, Rice, Trejo, Shaw-Williams and
  Chairman Springs.

Ms. Wilcox explained the appeals process.

7B. OVERVIEW REPORT ON FAST FOOD REGULATIONS.

Mr. Bernard McCrumby, Senior Planner, made the staff presentation.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff.

Commissioner Patrick made a statement to staff –
 I’d like to compliment Staff on the thorough and efficient Fast
  Food Code Amendment overview report. Time will not allow me to
  go into the zoning of fast food restaurants, the numbers of them
  here in Inglewood, the health of our residents, recently passed
  legislation designed to protect fast food workers, etc., etc.
  I am sure with some of my recent comments some may think that I
  am “anti-fast food” – I am not. I am against the over-
  proliferation here in Inglewood, generally and District One,
  specifically. I would like to suggest that with the completion
  of Phase-I of retail stores and restaurants as part of So-Fi,
  additional family-style, and dine-in restaurants will be
  developed here in the City of Inglewood. From a visual (no I
  will not give stats or details), fast food places are profitable
  and it is impossible to limit the number of people patronizing
  these restaurants, but I would like to suggest a “moratorium”
  on the approval of fast-food places until the completion of So-
  Fi Phase-I and the approval of a new code amendment.

Commissioner Rice made a statement to staff –
 Believes that another category should be added with regards to
  a more modern functioning kiosk and that would be an
  I.T./automation-type waiting staff system.

Commissioner Trejo asked questions and made a statement to staff-
 In looking at becoming consistent with all future applicants
  and if the City is serious in making these requirements, this
  action would be utilized in going forward, correct?
   Mr. McCrumby responded to Commissioner Trejo’s question.
 Say a Taco Bell were to come into the City, they would have to
  apply for a Special Use Permit, correct?
   Mr. McCrumby responded to Commissioner Trejo’s question.
 Only in the sense if there can be a separation clause installed
  as well, and will not affect the already established existing
  businesses, but for all new potential Fast Food considerations,
  correct?
   Mr. McCrumby responded to Commissioner Trejo’s question.
 As we can see that the drive-thru fast food restaurants are
  truly very profitable here in Inglewood every day, just look at

  5
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
March 1, 2023
  Starbucks, but I don’t want to be labeled as a City that only
  wants “hoity-toity” upscale style restaurants, to discourage
  low-end / small business Fast Food Restaurants, especially the
  mom & pop shops from attempting to open here, but that we are
  encouraging new businesses, regardless of what type of business
  you are attempting to open here, especially fast food.
   Mr. McCrumby responded to Commissioner Trejo’s statement.
   Mr. Jackson also responded to Commissioner Trejo’s statement.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams also made a statement to the applicant-
 Thank you Mr. Jackson for that explanation. I don’t know of any
  fast food restaurants that are within 500 feet of any schools
  in District four, I wanted to make a comment on a Clipper game
  I attended last night, and how proud I was that during half-
  time they recognized the owners of our local Inglewood
  Restaurants, Dulan’s, Sweet Red Peach, and Simply Wholesome,
  and how they were very well received from the attending
  audience/fans.
   Mr. McCrumby responded to Commissioner Shaw-Williams comment.

Commissioner Rice made an additional statement to staff –
 He noted that food delivery operations became successful in the
  Downtown Inglewood area, where mom and pop, small fast-food
  businesses have parking restricted for 15-20 minutes, and it
  helps them to stay afloat during the lack of attendance of sit-
  down customers.

Mr. Jackson also responded  to  Commissioner  Trejo  and  Commissioner
Patrick’s comment.

Commissioner Patrick made an additional statement –
 She stated that she understands Commissioner Trejo’s statement
  on not wanting Inglewood to become considered a non-fast food
  restaurant City, but doesn’t feel there is anything wrong with
  being a little “hoity-toity”, and having more sit-down family
  restaurants with white linen table cloths. It seems that this
  city can and should come up with a standard that will not
  alienate small mom and pop establishments. There is absolutely
  no reason why In & Out drive-thru restaurant that opens at
  11:00am every morning and to over twelve cars lined up
  immediately waiting to be serviced. This city needs additional
  sit-down restaurants to help with alleviating this congestion.

Chairman Springs stated to staff –
 Stated that possibly there could be a way that if one business
  moves away from a building, possibly there can be a way to stop
  it from turning into a fast food restaurant, but maybe there
  needs to be some changes with regards to where they may be
  located. In Los Angeles, on La Cienega, back in the day, it was
  known as Restaurant Row, where you could go for any type of food
  and sit-down to eat and engage in conversation with whomever
  you are with. A City could be labeled as a fast-food city and I
  don’t see anything wrong with that, especially with the So-Fi
  stadium and the new Clippers Arena that have and are being
  built, I don’t feel that there is anything particularly wrong
  with fast food, as it is great fit for those establishments. I
  feel that it is a fine line that we as a City can make work for
  everyone in the community.

Mr. McCrumby asked the Planning Commission for feedback on proposed
Fast Food Regulations?

  6
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
March 1, 2023
Commissioner Trejo made a statement to staff –
 Yes it is a fine line that will have to be considered, but in
  the past, when Hollywood Park first set out with regards to
  their new project, they were going to have sit-down, white table
  cloths, food-court type of option, similar to the San Francisco
  Ferry Building and I feel that would be considered a plus for
  the City and I would not want to alienate anything like that,
  where you would go to a counter, order your meal and retrieve
  it when it is ready for pick-up, because it is also considered
  fast food, right?!

Mr. McCrumby responded to both Chairman Springs and Commissioner
Trejo’s statements.

Mr. McCrumby also asked the Planning Commission if they would like
to have come before them prior to the opening of drive-thrus to
consider conditions related to cueing, outdoor speakers, and
distance between fast-food restaurants. He also stated that not
all fast food is unhealthy, for example Tender Greens, and other
Health-based restaurants that we have been attempting to attract
here in Inglewood.

Chairman Springs also commented that –
 One of our major concerns is the number of franchises in the
  City, there is McDonalds, Jack-in-the-Box, and Starbucks, just
  to name a few, and possibly we may need to put a limit on the
  number of locations here in the City.

Commissioner Patrick made a comment to staff –
 Stated that it’s true, some of the franchises are attempting to
  sell salads and as you might notice, those sales are not very
  popular. Also with regards to some of the drive-thru locations,
  especially at the location on 8th Avenue and Crenshaw Blvd.,
  where the drive-thru alone is so small that many of the vehicles
  today can’t fit through the narrow space provided and some of
  the trucks have even had to back-out of the drive-thru. This
  has caused several vehicles/trucks to back onto the major
  thoroughfare.

Commissioner Rice made a comment to staff –
 Stated that with regards to the drive-thru by-right that the
  franchises are taking full advantage of, maybe that needs to be
  looked at in the code and changed.
 Also, the drive-thru problems might have to do with the curb-
  cuts which might need to be enlarged.
   Mr. Jackson responded to Commissioner Patrick’s and
  Commissioner Rice’s comments.

Commissioner Rice also stated to staff –
 Possibly the City could work on acquiring culturally-based
  different types of mom and pop styled restaurants (where the
  community would not have to go outside of the area to obtain
  such delicacies of other regions and nationalities), these
  smaller shops can be within the 300 to 400 square-foot radius,
  they can thrive and prosper and the community would benefit from
  this as well, this is something we should look into and consider.

  7
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
March 1, 2023
Commissioner Trejo also had a statement for staff –
 Stated  she  noticed  that  several  of  the  fast-food
  franchises/establishments are good for the local residents in
  looking for great employment opportunities as an excellent
  starting point for youth, single parents, and seniors and in
  not wanting to discourage this opportunity for the community.
 I personally have a choice where I want to go, whether it is in
  our city or in Manhattan Beach.

Mr. Jackson gave a closing statement in commending the Planning
Commissioners, especially Commissioner Trejo who mentioned how
these fast-food establishments provide additional employment
opportunities within the community. Also commending the planning
staff on doing an exceptional job at giving the Planning Commission
full information and an excellent presentation on this Fast Food
Overview.

Chairman Springs closed the non-public hearing.

(8) PUBLIC COMMENTS:
None.

(9) COMMISSION INITIATIVES:
Commissioner Patrick –
 Wanted to say thank you for this evenings meeting and
  especially of course regarding Item 7B, and to say thank you
  to staff.
 Wanted to talk about CicLAvia — Mid City meets Pico Union
  presented by Metro, as a former member herself, rode in
  Cerritos last week and the fact that with everything that is
  happening here in Inglewood, why not join-in with this group
  which travels all over, as it is a fun event for children and
  adults alike who ride bikes, roller skates, skate-boarding,,
  etc.

Commissioner Rice –
 Hollywood Park will be hosting and celebrating a Hip-Hop event
  here in Inglewood at So-Fi on March 3rd, 4th, and 5th. The
  streets will be crowded with thousands of people and full of
  a lot of traffic. Everyone will need to plan their movement

Commissioner Trejo –
 Wanted to also say that she agrees with Commissioner Patrick
  and staff that this was a very good Planning Commission
  meeting. The overview and presentations were great and the back
  and forth discussion regarding the events and things that are
  happening here to the City and how all of the Commission’s
  staff works excellently and really hard on everyone’s behalf.
  She stated also thank you to Parks and Recreation and also
  Public Works for doing a great job with keeping this City going
  forward. Thank you all once again.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams -
 Wanting to send Congratulations to the Public Works and Parks
  and Recreation Departments on the excellent job they did in
  celebrating Black History Month in February, and the MLK
  Festival that was held on the 18th here in Inglewood, had a
  marvelous time and thank you.

Chairman Springs –
 Concurring with his colleague Commissioner Shaw-Williams

 This month, March has been designated “Women’s Month”, in

 Wanted to thank staff for all of the wonderful work they have
